newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: First Austria takes majority stake in GiroCredit.
newsitem.headline: First Austria takes majority stake in GiroCredit.

text.p: First Austrian bank sealed a 8.24 billion schillings acquisition of a 56.1 percent stake in GiroCredit Bank AG on Wednesday to form Austria's second biggest banking group.

The deal between First Austrian, the nation's oldest savings bank, and Vienna City holding company AVZ comes hot on the heels of market leader Bank Austria's acquisition in January of rival Creditanstalt.
Analysts forecast at the time that deal would lead to more mergers in the nation's overcrowded banking sector.
"The entire country and its economy emerge as winners from this transaction," First Austrian chief executive Konrad Fuchs told journalists after signing the contract.
Earlier the supervisory board of First Austrian unanimously backed the acquisition which raises First Austrian's GiroCredit holding to 82 percent of ordinary capital.
"First Austrian has created an excellent framework for the formation of a new, strong Austrian banking group," it said in a statement.

Pending cartel authority approval, First Austrian will pay 400 schillings for each of AVZ's 20.6 million ordinary GiroCredit shares, representing 51.1 percent of total capital. The money is payable on March 31, 1998.
First Austrian said it expected to carry out a capital increase to finance the deal in the coming months.
GiroCredit ordinary shares are unlisted. Its preferred stock closed at 316 schillings on Wednesday. First Austrian preferred were steady at 523.

AVZ, which controls Bank Austria, agreed to sell its GiroCredit interest under the terms of a complicated political agreement, struck in January, that awarded Bank Austria the state's majority Creditanstalt holding.
With combined assets of around 650 billion schillings, First Austrian and GiroCredit will rank among Europe's top 70 banks and the top 150 worldwide.
Together they employ 8,500 staff in 370 domestic branches and more than a dozen foreign outlets.
"The new group will be represented in all important world financial centres and have one of the densest branch networks in Austria," First Austrian said.
"It is our aim to raise the significance and market position of the savings bank sector and make it more competitive in the future European market."
Analysts gave the deal a cautious welcome but expressed some surprise at what they considered a high price.
"First Austria is one of the nation's more efficient banks. I would imagine its cooperation with GiroCredit will be more successful than Bank Austria's," said an international analyst.
"But I am a little surprised they appear to be paying more for GiroCredit than they were willing to pay for a stake in Creditanstalt."
First Austrian was part of an international consortium that lost out to Bank Austria in the race for Creditanstalt at the eleventh hour.
First Austrian board member Andreas Treichl, who succeeds Andreas Fuchs as chief executive on July 1, said it remained open whether the two banks would merge.
"Over the next weeks and months we will work with GiroCredit, investment banks and auditors to find the most profitable path," he said.
